title: Cross‑language retry ergonomics: conservative defaults, idempotency cost model, and recoverable error taxonomy
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Goal: Define conservative, production-safe retry/backoff defaults and cross-SDK idempotency semantics that minimize accidental duplicate side effects while being ergonomically simple for Python, TypeScript, and Go clients. Outcome must include a small taxonomy of retryable vs non-retryable errors, a recommended default policy per call class (idempotent, non-idempotent, streaming), simple guidance for idempotency key usage (TTL, key placement, server dedup window), and concrete examples for each SDK. Constraints: keep API surface minimal, avoid changing public method signatures beyond optional client config, and provide a safe rollout plan (feature flag + telemetry).
acceptance_criteria: A single documented default RetryPolicy shipped in each SDK with conservative numeric defaults and clear overrides
Idempotency header documented and implemented consistently: 'Idempotency-Key' for unary calls, guidance for streaming semantics
A concise retryable-error taxonomy included in SDK docs and used by the default policy implementation
Unit and integration tests for backoff and idempotency behavior across Python/TS/Go
Migration/rollout plan with telemetry hooks to measure duplicate side-effects and retry frequency
technical_decision_log: 2026-03-01: Decided to centralize RetryPolicy object in core SDK layer rather than per-method wrappers to simplify client config across languages.

2026-03-03: Adopt conservative defaults: max_retries=5 for idempotent unary, max_retries=1 for non-idempotent on safe transient errors, streaming resumptions use resumable tokens rather than aggressive retries.
2026-03-05: Chose three error categories: retryable_transient, retryable_idempotent_only, non_retryable_permanent. Mapping rules documented below.
2026-03-08: Agreed on server-side deduplication window recommendation (~24h) but make it a suggestion; client TTL guidance set to 7d for long-lived idempotency keys when explicitly used by customers.
implementation_notes: Add a core RetryPolicy class in core package for Python/TS/Go with fields: max_retries, initial_backoff_ms, max_backoff_ms, multiplier, jitter(true/false), retry_on_http_5xx(boolean for idempotent), and apply_to_streams(enum: none, resumable).

Default numeric settings: idempotent_unary => {max_retries: 5, initial_backoff_ms: 100, multiplier: 2.0, max_backoff_ms: 5000, jitter: true}; non_idempotent_unary => {max_retries: 1, initial_backoff_ms: 200, multiplier: 1.5, max_backoff_ms: 2000, jitter: true}; streaming => resumable token flow (no aggressive automatic retries of in-flight frames).

HTTP/gRPC mapping (used by default classifier): HTTP 429, 502, 503, 504 => retryable_transient; HTTP 500 => retryable_idempotent_only (server may be transient); HTTP 409, 400 => non_retryable_permanent; gRPC UNAVAILABLE, DEADLINE_EXCEEDED => retryable_transient; INTERNAL => idempotent_only. This is conservative and can be overridden by callers.

Idempotency header: clients SHOULD set 'Idempotency-Key' on operations that may have side effects when customers opt-in; SDKs will expose a helper IdempotencyKey.generate(prefix) which creates v4 UUID prefixed tokens. Document server dedup window recommendation and client TTL guidance.

Streaming ergonomics: For long-running streams (server->client tokens / delta updates) provide a StreamResumeToken in SDK response wrapper. For client->server streaming with side effects, recommend application-level explicit checkpoints rather than automatic retries.
test_plan: Unit tests: backoff math, jitter distribution, max retries enforcement across SDKs
Integration tests using testserver: inject status codes (429, 500, 503, 409) and assert retry behavior differs for idempotent vs non-idempotent calls
Streaming tests: simulate mid-stream connection drop and validate resume token flow restores stream offset without duplicating side effects
Chaos tests: simulate flapping backend to ensure we do not overload origin during retry storms (verify client respects max_backoff_ms and jitter)
Telemetry: emit metrics for retry_count, retry_reason, idempotency_key_present, and duplicate_detection_events to measure safety during rollout
comments: 2026-03-02 (Aisha): Initial draft posted. Asking for engineering + SDK leads to review numeric defaults and error mappings.

2026-03-04 (Marco - SDK lead): Recommend lowering idempotent_unary max_retries to 4 for latency-sensitive mobile clients; suggest making jitter the default across languages. Assigned Daniel to prototype in Python.
2026-03-06 (Daniel): Python prototype implemented. Verified backoff behavior with local testserver. Pushed PR for python-core: https://github.com/redwood-inference/python-sdk/pull/312 (WIP).
2026-03-07 (Priya - TS SDK): TypeScript helper API naming suggestion: RetryPolicy vs RetryConfig; prefer RetryConfig to align with existing clientOptions pattern. Will update TS PR accordingly.

2026-03-09 (Security): reviewed idempotency header guidance; no secrets should be placed in idempotency keys. Recommend default generator produce unpredictible UUIDs only. Marking security_review_required=false.

2026-03-10 (Daniel): Updated title and moved to In Review. Requesting PM + design sign-off on docstrings and public API ergonomics before merging across languages. Next: finalize Go examples and add typed telemetry events.
python_example:
Python example:
from redwood import RedwoodClient, RetryPolicy
client = RedwoodClient(client_options={'retry_policy': RetryPolicy(max_retries=5, initial_backoff_ms=100, multiplier=2.0)})
resp = client.generate(prompt='charge card', idempotency_key='user-1234-pay-202603')
go_example:
Go example:
import "github.com/redwood-inference/go-sdk"
client := sdk.NewClient(sdk.ClientOptions{ RetryPolicy: sdk.RetryPolicy{MaxRetries:5, InitialBackoffMs:100, Multiplier:2.0}})
resp, err := client.Generate(ctx, sdk.GenerateParams{Prompt: "charge card", IdempotencyKey: "user-1234-pay-202603"})
rollout_plan: Feature-flag rollout in SDK core: 1) behind feature flag default-on in canary builds, 2) collect telemetry for 2 weeks in canary orgs only, 3) expand to all new SDK releases after duplicate side-effect rate <= 0.01% for two consecutive weeks, 4) expose opt-out at client creation time.
notes_for_docs: Public docs must include: simple one-line summary of default behavior, examples for adding Idempotency-Key in each language, explanation of retry categories and when to override defaults, and a short troubleshooting section for duplicate side-effects with recommended mitigations.
